name: The Caro-Kann Defense
description: The rock-solid counterpunch for Black against 1. e4. Prepare an unshakeable pawn structure, strike in the center, and easily activate all minor pieces.

chapters.title: Classical Variation (3. Nc3 dxe4)
chapters.subtitle: Countering White's open center assault with 4... Bf5

steps.title: White Claims Center
steps.explanation: White takes the center with e4, preparing active piece play.

steps.title: The Caro-Kann Setup
steps.explanation: The signature move of the Caro-Kann! We prepare to challenge White's e4 pawn with ...d5 on our next move, supported by the c6 pawn.

steps.title: White Builds Full Center
steps.explanation: White occupies the center with both pawns (d4 and e4).

steps.title: Strike at e4
steps.explanation: Boom! We strike the center. White must now decide how to react.

steps.title: The Classical Setup
steps.explanation: White develops a Knight and guards the e4 pawn.

steps.title: Eliminate the e4 Pawn
steps.explanation: We capture on e4! White is forced to recapture with their Knight, freeing up the c8-h3 diagonal for our Bishop.

steps.title: White Recaptures
steps.explanation: White brings their Knight to a strong central outpost on e4.

steps.title: The Free Bishop!
steps.explanation: We develop our light-squared Bishop with tempo by attacking White's e4 knight. This is the ultimate dream of the Caro-Kann — our bishop is active outside the pawn chain before we play ...e6!

chapters.title: Advance Variation (3. e5 Bf5!)
chapters.subtitle: Handling White's 3. e5 space grab by developing the Bishop first

steps.title: 1. e4
steps.explanation: White opens with e4.

steps.title: Caro-Kann
steps.explanation: Prepare ...d5.

steps.title: 2. d4
steps.explanation: Full center.

steps.title: 2... d5
steps.explanation: Strike the center.

steps.title: 3. e5 Advance
steps.explanation: White grabs space.

steps.title: Activate the Bishop First!
steps.explanation: Crucial distinction! In the French Defense, the bishop is trapped behind e6. In the Caro-Kann, we bring our bishop OUT to f5 FIRST, before locking down with ...e6 and ...c5!
steps.warning: Never play 3... e6? first — you lose the entire point of the Caro-Kann!

chapters.title: Playing as White (Panov-Botvinnik Attack)
chapters.subtitle: How White destroys Black's pawn structure with 4. c4!

steps.title: Pawn to e4
steps.explanation: We open.

steps.title: Black plays Caro-Kann
steps.explanation: Black prepares d5.

steps.title: Build Center
steps.explanation: Take the center.

steps.title: Black strikes
steps.explanation: Black challenges e4.

steps.title: Exchange Pawns
steps.explanation: We trade off our e4 pawn.

steps.title: Black Recaptures
steps.explanation: Black keeps their pawn on d5.

steps.title: The Panov-Botvinnik Attack!
steps.explanation: The most aggressive weapon for White against the Caro-Kann! We immediately strike Black's d5 pawn with c4, turning a quiet Caro-Kann into a dynamic, open IQP attacking game!
